title: interactive-hint-strip-wireframe-annotated
content:
Context and purpose

Quick, rough writeup for a low-friction UI pattern we want to prototype in Optimize: an "interactive hint strip" — a thin, persistent row inside the Console that surface 1–2 prioritized prescriptive recommendations (batching / caching / quantization) with a small details drawer and fast action buttons. Goal is to get teams to apply low-risk optimizations with minimal cognitive overhead and to make impact visible (estimated token savings + quick simulate).

Why this pattern?
- Product gap: users see long recommendation lists and avoid action because they need to jump between pages to understand impact.
- Hypothesis: a low-attention strip reduces friction and increases conversion of recommendation -> applied configuration.
- Constraints: must be compact, performance-neutral, and fail-safe (no surprise model changes).

High-level behavior (wireframe notes)
1) Location + visibility
 - Primary placement: top of the route/model config page (below route header) and also visible on the Recs list view header when there is an active route selected.
 - The strip shows when Optimize has >=1 high-confidence recommendation OR when the user has explicitly enabled proactive hints.
2) Compact card elements
 - Each hint is a pill/card (max 2 visible) with: icon (batch/cache/quantize), short copy (6–9 words), estimated 7-day token savings (icon + number), and two actions: [Preview] and [Apply].
 - Tapping the card expands a small inline drawer anchored below the card (max 320px width) that shows: rationale, expected latency delta, estimated quality delta (Q-score), telemetry sample link, and a small simulation toggle.
3) Preview flow
 - Preview opens the drawer; runs a lightweight dry-run simulation against a cached prompt sample set (user-selectable) and displays a mini-chart: tokens before vs after, latency distribution, and a short example snippet showing altered output (if quantization changes).
4) Apply flow
 - Apply triggers a staged change: it creates a pending config change (named {hint-short}-{date}) and opens a small modal with three options: [Apply now - with canary], [Schedule], [Save as draft].
 - Canary: default to 10% traffic on Same-Region variant for 24h, auto-fallback to previous config on error/regressions. Canary parameters are editable in the modal.
5) Undo / quick rollback
 - Every applied change is tracked with a one-click rollback from the strip (shows last applied action and its status).

UX copy drafts (short)
- Batching hint pill: "Enable request batching — save ~12% tokens"
- Caching hint pill: "Turn on prefix caching — faster responses for repeated prompts"
- Quantization hint pill: "Try 8-bit quantization — lower cost, small perf tradeoff"
In-drawer small help copy: "Estimates are based on your recent traffic patterns and our model-quality guardrails. Preview runs on anonymized sample traffic."

Telemetry and signals to capture (engineering note)
- Event names: rec_strip_shown, rec_strip_clicked, rec_preview_requested, rec_apply_started, rec_apply_completed, rec_canary_started, rec_rollback_triggered, rec_preview_sim_result.
- Critical metrics: apply conversion %, preview -> apply conversion, average token savings/week, QoE regression rate (alerts), rollback rate, canary failure rate.

Acceptance criteria (MVP)
- UI renders strip when at least one high-confidence rec exists for current route.
- Clicking Preview shows drawer and runs simulation against default sample set (bounded runtime < 5s).
- Apply flows create a pending config change and can start a canary (10% default).
- Telemetry events emitted for preview/apply/rollback.
- Admins can disable strip at org level from Optimize settings.

Edge cases and safety
- If the simulation fails or times out, show a concise error and an option to retry.
- Quantization recs must pass a quality guardrail threshold before appearing (linked to model eval service).
- For routes serving PII or regulated data, strip must not propose caching recommendations unless customer explicitly enabled caching for that route.

Wireframe annotations (what to hand to design)
- Default collapsed state: single-line strip with 2 cards and a chevron for more.
- Expanded state: inline drawer anchored to card; drawer includes: 1) small chart (tokens/latency), 2) two example prompts with before/after outputs, 3) quick risk meter (green/amber/red) computed by backend.
- Modal: compact, with canary slider (5–50%), schedule field, and a checkbox: "Run evaluation on holdout set before canary".

Backlog grooming — implementation tasks (rough prioritization)
1) Backend: expose recs endpoint that returns: rec_id, type, estimated_savings_pct, confidence_score, required_guardrails, preview_sample_ids. (3 wks)
2) Simulation API: lightweight dry-run that accepts sample_ids and rec_id, returns tokens_before/after, latency_estimates, sample_output_diffs. (2 wks)
3) Frontend: strip component + drawer + modal + telemetry hooks. (2 sprints)
4) Canary plumbing: reuse existing rollout infra; add auto-fallback and rollback UI hooks. (1 sprint)
5) Admin flag: org-level toggle + per-route override. (0.5 sprint)
6) UX research: 5 customer sessions with prototype + success metrics. (ongoing)

Open questions / tradeoffs
- How aggressive should default recommended batching targets be? (tradeoff: latency vs cost). Proposal: show conservative default and have a confidence slider in drawer for "aggressive" suggestions.
- Should Preview run on live traffic or anonymized cached samples? Recommendation: default to cached/anonymized sample set with option to run on a live traffic snapshot if user enables it.
- Level of detail in strip: minimal or slightly richer? Risk: cognitive overload vs discoverability. Start minimal, add an "expand for detail" affordance.

Design experiments + metric plan
- A/B test: baseline (no strip) vs strip-on for new active users on Optimize. Primary metric: rec_apply_rate per route. Secondary: rollback_rate, avg_token_savings, user time-to-first-apply.
- Success threshold: 4x increase in apply_rate with rollback_rate < 5% in first 30 days.

Prototype notes and where to find assets
- Figma: https://figma.com/file/xyz-interactive-hint-strip (working prototype with 3 states)
- Mock data set: optimize-recs/sample-sets/v1 (used for simulations)

Next steps (owner: Aisha)
- Sync with Applied ML on simulation cost and sample sets (by 2025-02-20).
- Design: produce hi-fi frames for collapsed/expanded/modal states (by 2025-02-28).
- Engineering: spike on simulation API latency and add initial telemetry schema (by 2025-03-07).

Notes to self / minutes from 2025-02-18 sync
- Marco: pushed to ensure quant recs are gated by model evals.
- Sana: flagged privacy constraint for caching recs; product should respect per-route data class.
- Jon: will plumb rec telemetry into Console tracing for debugging.

Rough acceptance checklist for staging demo
- [ ] Strip renders with sample recs in staging.
- [ ] Preview runs and shows tokens chart.
- [ ] Apply creates pending config and can start canary.
- [ ] Telemetry events visible in debug logs.

Unresolved
- Need to finalize default canary size and schedule policy (owner: SRE/Platform).
- Decide whether the strip shows quant recs for models running on Dedicated vs Hosted by default.

End of draft.
